target: Huset ska säljas under sommaren nästa år.
english: The house is going to be sold during the summer next year.
tip: "Ska säljas" = will be sold. Modal + infinitive s-passive. Very common in real estate.
The -s ending can mark a passive or a deponent (active meaning). Here träffas is deponent: it means meet each other, not is met.
Liknas takes vid, not av, for the thing compared to. Hon liknas vid sin mamma = she is likened to her mother.

target: De turas om att laga mat.
tip: Turas om means take turns. It is a set phrase: turas om att laga mat = take turns cooking.

target: Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe.
tip: Skulle vilja is the polite would like, softer than vill (want). Jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe.

target: En överraskande nyhet väldigt ofta nu.
english: A surprising piece of news very often now.
tip: "Överraskande" (surprising) – present participle (-ande/-ende) never inflects. Same for all forms.

target: Om vi hade pengar skulle vi resa.
english: If we had money we would travel.
tip: For a hypothetical, use past tense after om and skulle in the result: om vi hade pengar skulle vi resa.

target: Välkommen till Sverige, jag hoppas att du trivs bra här.
english: Welcome to Sweden, I hope you enjoy it here.
tip: 'Hoppas' (to hope) – deponent verb ending in -s but with active meaning.

english: The document was approved by the boss.
tip: In a passive, av names the doer, like English by. Godkändes av chefen means approved by the boss.

english: The car was stolen last night.
tip: Bli plus a past participle is a second passive. Blev stulen stresses a single completed event, unlike the -s passive.

target: De andas tungt efter löpningen ibland till slut.
english: They breathe heavily after the run sometimes in the end.
tip: "Andas" is deponent – always has -s but is active in meaning (to breathe).
"Brottas" = wrestle. Reciprocal – they wrestle each other.
Fattas is deponent and takes the missing thing as its subject: han fattas mig means he is missing to me.
The -s ending plus åt makes a verb reciprocal: vi följdes åt = we went along with each other.
Umgås exists only in the -s form and means to spend time together. There is no plain umga: vi umgås = we socialize.
Use det finns for both there is and there are, whatever the number: det finns många sjöar = there are many lakes.

english: I am touched by the music.
tip: The -s ending can form a passive, and av marks the doer: jag berörs av musiken = I am touched by the music.
Skulle kunna plus an infinitive means could or would be able to: jag skulle kunna hjälpa = I could help.
Kommer att plus an infinitive is the plain future: det kommer att bli dyrt = it will be expensive.

english: It turns out to be true.
tip: Visar sig means turns out or proves to be, and the sig is required: det visar sig vara sant = it turns out to be true.

target: Jag skulle inte ha gjort det.
tip: For the past conditional use skulle ha plus the supine form: skulle inte ha gjort = would not have done.

target: I gengäld hjälper jag dig imorgon.
english: In return, I'll help you tomorrow.
tip: When a phrase like i gengäld opens the clause, the verb still stays second and the subject follows: i gengäld hjälper jag.

english: We'll meet at half past four.
tip: Halv fem means half to five, that is 4:30, not 5:30. Swedish counts down toward the coming hour.

english: We always succeed in the end.
tip: Lyckas ends in -s but is active, not passive: vi lyckas means we succeed, not we are succeeded. It only exists in this -s form.

english: On the other hand, I like coffee.
tip: Front an adverb like däremot and the verb moves ahead of the subject: däremot gillar jag, not däremot jag gillar.
Oroa sig (to worry) is reflexive; the pronoun tracks the subject, so with du you say oroa dig, with jag oroa mig.
"Kommer att bli" = will become/get. "Bli" is the go-to verb for changes of state.
The -s on ses makes it reciprocal: see each other. The same trick gives träffas (meet) and hörs (talk soon).
Skulle plus a bare verb like göra expresses would, a hypothetical: han skulle göra det, not something he actually did.
Skulle ha stannat covers both a neutral would have stayed and a regretful should have stayed. Context tells you which one is meant.
